column1: # writes outside a WithTransaction closure and has no entry here. Seeded from
# Session O's O1 triage (~/proj/prompts/reports/SESSION-O.md) — every hit from
# the coordinator's txscan (32) plus the blind-spot core-to-core sweep (6) was
# individually read and classified before being listed.
# Rows whose function field starts with "AUDIT:" instead belong to
# scratch/txscan2): a SUCCESS audit event that textually precedes a later
# storage write in the same function. Kept as a distinct key namespace (not
# a plain function-name row) because the SAME function can legitimately need
# both a write-count exemption above AND an audit-before-write exemption
# here, for unrelated reasons (see handleSessionReuse/RevokeLease, which have
# both). There is no equivalent for TestAtomicityGuard_TransactionEscape
# (ESCAPE) — that check is never exemptable; see its own doc comment.
#   B — consume-first by design: a single-use value is consumed BEFORE later
#       work and must stay consumed even if later work fails (replay
#       protection). See the function's own `// atomicity: consume-first by
#       design` comment and its verifying test (Session O, O4).
#   C — independent steps by design: partial completion is safe and
#       self-healing (a later run/retry naturally corrects it).
#   D — false positive: the flagged calls are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches
#       (if/else, switch) — never actually sequential — or the function is
#       already atomic via a single storage primitive with the flagged calls
#   S — saga (compensating-action): no single DB transaction is available
#       (the writes span audited, individually-locked core choke points like
#       AssignUserRole/RemoveUserRole, not raw storage calls), so the function
#       instead tracks what succeeded and reverts it on a later failure, with
#       the revert's own failure audited loudly. Reviewed and accepted as this
#       codebase's established alternative to a DB transaction for this shape
#   TEMP-A — a genuine, confirmed class-A atomicity bug (must be fixed, not
#       exempted) with an OPEN, NOT-YET-MERGED fix PR already up. Listed here
#       ONLY so this guard can be merged without immediately breaking CI on
#       unfixed main — remove the line as part of merging the cited PR (the
#       fix wraps the writes in WithTransaction, so the function naturally
#       stops being flagged once merged; the TSV line becomes dead weight, not
#       actively wrong, if left — but should be cleaned up).
# Rows whose function field starts with "JIT:" are a third key namespace, for a
# function that needs a SECOND, independent classification because two
# unrelated groups of writes inside it were reviewed separately. The namespace
# exists for the same reason "AUDIT:" does, and is NOT optional: both readers
# key a plain row on the function name alone and keep the LAST one, so a second
# plain row for an already-listed function would silently RECLASSIFY it --
# which, for a class-B function, would break the oracle exemption that rests on
# requires B). A "JIT:" row documents without shadowing. Both readers now also
# refuse a duplicate key outright, so this cannot be got wrong silently.
# Never add a class-A (real, unfixed, no-open-PR) entry here. Fix it instead.

column3: #2295 merged 2026-09-29: the real bootstrap path now runs entirely inside one WithTransaction (tx.* calls, correctly invisible to this scan), with LogUserCreated/LogProjectCreated audited only after commit. The 2 remaining c.storage calls this guard sees are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches: SetSystemMetadata (the "total > 0" backfill case for a pre-fix install, which returns immediately after) and AddPasswordHistory (the post-commit best-effort seed in the actual first-boot path) -- the backfill branch never reaches the password-history line. Re-verify this class if #2246 (still open at review time; adds its own audit-ordering changes on top of #2295) touches this function's control flow.
Per-type purge batches, independently `rec()`'d, self-healing next scheduled run.

MFA challenge + WebAuthn session consumed before mintSession; trailing UpsertMFAStepupToken/CreateMFAStepUpGrant are best-effort UX convenience post-mint. Verified fail-closed: TestFinishWebAuthnLogin_MintFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (Session O, O4, PR #2310).
Same shape as FinishWebAuthnLoginPending. Verified: TestFinishWebAuthnPasswordlessLogin_MintFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (Session O, O4, PR #2310).
The 2 DeleteSession calls are on mutually exclusive early-return branches (ceiling exceeded / account inactive); RotateSession is already one atomic CAS transaction (#211).

Challenge consumed first; TOTP vs recovery-code are mutually exclusive attempts. Verified: TestVerifyMFALogin_MintFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed exercises this via its caller VerifyMFALogin (Session O, O4, PR #2310).
TOTP attempt then recovery-code attempt, consume-shaped. Verified: TestVerifyMFAStepUp_GrantFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (Session O, O4, PR #2310).

CreateBreakGlassActivation then assignUserRoleWithExpirySkipSoD; on grant failure the activation is reconciled back to revoked (compensating revert), with the revert's own failure now audited loudly (Session O, O3 item 5, PR #2307). Renamed from (*KeyorixCore).ActivateBreakGlass by #2722, which extracted this exact write pair into a helper so both run under one projectAdminGuardLockKey acquisition -- the writes, the compensating revert and therefore the class S reasoning are unchanged; only the enclosing function name moved.
The 2 UpdateDynamicSecretLease calls are on mutually exclusive branches (engine.Revoke fails -> revoke_failed; succeeds -> revoked).

Grants role, then records approval, then updates request state; a compensating revert (RemoveUserRole) now covers every failure after the grant lands, not only the original !ok race (Session O, O3 item 4, PR #2306).
The 2 SetSecretCertNotAfter calls are on mutually exclusive branches (cert parses / doesn't).

MarkTOTPStepUsed / ConsumeMFAStepUpGrant are alternative verification paths, consume-shaped. Verified: existing TestRequireReauth_GrantConsumedOnFirstAction_SecondDifferentActionRejected and siblings (mfa_stepup_grant_single_use_test.go); re-confirmed in scope during Session O, O4, PR #2310. Scope note (ORACLE-A-1, 2026-10-05): consumes NOTHING when called from ActivateMFA -- activation runs with user.MFAEnabled still false, so secondFactorEnrolled is false and the bare-password branch is taken. ActivateMFA's own row below covers that path; do not attribute ActivateMFA's burned LastUsedStep to this function.

Its OWN MarkTOTPStepUsed (internal/core/mfa.go, not requireReauth's -- see that row's scope note) burns the matched enrolment-code time-step BEFORE the activation transaction, and must stay burned if that transaction fails, or a stolen enrolment code is replayable inside its +/-1-step window. Verified: TestActivateMFA_ActivationFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (consume_first_fails_closed_test.go), red/green-proved -- its red proof folds the consume into the transaction and shows the replay then succeeds. Added by ORACLE-A-1 (2026-10-05) after coordinator review on PR #2840 found the oracle exemption for REST POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/activate citing requireReauth, which does not perform this consumption. Also consumed by server/faultops' consumeFirstExemptions via TestConsumeFirstExemptions_MatchAtomicityLedger, which requires this row to read B.
force/non-force branches are mutually exclusive; the non-force path already uses DeleteProjectIfEmpty, a single atomic storage primitive (#528).
The 2 UpdateAccessRequest calls are on mutually exclusive branches (lazy-expire vs approve); grants no role at all.
CreateUserWithRoleGrants is already one atomic storage call (user+grants together); AddPasswordHistory after is deliberately best-effort per ADR-025 (self-healing on next password change).

The 2 flagged UpdateUserIfActiveStateMatches calls are on mutually exclusive switch branches; the deactivating branch's own PAT/session revocation is already correctly WithTransaction-wrapped, with the revocation sub-calls' best-effort-ness explicitly justified (ValidateSessionToken/ValidatePATToken independently re-check IsActive on every use).

DeleteSession (legacy, no-family) / DeleteSessionsByFamily are on mutually exclusive branches. The real gap here was a swallowed single-write error, not multi-write atomicity — fixed by auditing loudly on DeleteSessionsByFamily failure (Session O, O2 item 2, PR #2298); the branch shape itself is unchanged and still textually flagged.

ConsumeWebAuthnSession before CreateMFAStepUpGrant; fails closed (grant-creation failure returns an error with the session already consumed and no grant issued). Verified: TestFinishWebAuthnReauth_GrantFailureAfterConsume_FailsClosed (Session O, O4, PR #2310) — no prior test existed for this function at all.
Independent per-rule alert saves, failure count aggregated, not fatal.

Password hash + account-state ARE already correctly transactional. The 2 flagged writes are the best-effort tail: AddPasswordHistory (reuse-policy only, self-healing) and RevokeAllPersonalAccessTokensForUser (security-relevant; its failure is now audited loudly rather than silently swallowed — Session O, O2 item 2, PR #2298).
switch on d.PrincipalType — mutually exclusive branches (group/machine/user).
switch on the upstream backend-rotation result — mutually exclusive branches; already has an explicit partial-state audit trail (ROTATION-001).

Per-item body of BulkDeleteSecrets' loop (extracted so a panic on one item can be recovered without losing earlier items' results); each item's fetch+delete is independent, failures collected in the result rather than aborting the batch — correct design for a bulk operation.

Membership-state write then role-grant side effect; revertFailedActivation (audits loudly, "MANUAL CLEANUP REQUIRED", on its own failure) covers both the activate and revoke directions, including the benign ErrNotProjectMember case. Reference-quality saga pattern for this codebase.

Full role-set replacement via AssignUserRole/RemoveUserRole (each its own audited choke point, no shared DB transaction available); tracks what landed and reverts it on any later failure, with the revert's own failure audited loudly (Session O, O3 item 7, PR #2309). New finding, not in the coordinator's original 32-hit list — found via the core-to-core blind-spot sweep this guard's corescan half now covers permanently.

Reclassified from the coordinator's preliminary "A": verified ValidateSessionToken/ValidatePATToken BOTH independently re-check IsActive/AccountLoginBlocked on every use, cold path and the warm-cache path, so a failed revocation here leaves only an inert row, never a live credential — self-healing, not a real gap. See SESSION-O.md's O1 table for the full verification.

ConsumeSSOLoginState (single-use login state, replay protection) is consumed before mintSession; the trailing RecordLogin is an explicitly-commented best-effort last-login stamp. Fails closed by construction: a mintSession failure returns an error with the login state already consumed. New finding — a mixed storage-write + core-to-core-write shape invisible to a scanner that only counts one call style at a time (this guard's own historical txscan/corescan split would each have seen only 1 write here, not 2+).

Andrei's decision on #2839 item 1 (2026-10-09): the JIT-provisioning and group/role-reconciliation writes are class C -- independent, self-healing steps -- a SEPARATE classification from the class-B row above, which by its own stated reason covers only the ConsumeSSOLoginState consumption and deliberately does not stretch to User/UserGroup/UserRole. Self-healing because provisionSSOUser and reconcileSSOGroups/reconcileSSORoles are each idempotent and converge on the next successful login, and because a half-applied run leaves a USABLE account rather than a corrupt one: nothing is half-written, the account simply has not logged in yet. Accepted WITH three conditions, each enforced by a test that is red when broken, in internal/core/saml_jit_class_c_test.go -- (1) mintSession runs only if provisionSSOUser AND both reconciles fully succeeded; any error means no session (TestCompleteSAML_GroupReconcileReadFailureRefusesTheLogin, _FailedGroupRemovalRefusesTheLogin, _RoleReconcileReadFailureRefusesTheLogin, with _CleanReconcileStillMintsASession as the calibration that stops the condition being met by refusing everything); (2) reconcile removes as well as adds and derives roles only from the validated assertion (_ReconcileRemovesAsWellAsAdds, _RolesDerivedOnlyFromTheValidatedAssertion); (3) JIT account creation is audited even when the login then fails (_JITProvisionIsAuditedEvenWhenTheLoginThenFails). Condition 1 did NOT hold before this row: both reconcile calls returned nothing and swallowed every error, so a failed REVOCATION -- the IdP drops a user from its admin group and the removal errors or is refused -- left the privilege in place and still minted a session. Fixed in the same PR; class C is only sound WITH that fix, since the sole protection against a half-applied reconcile is refusing to mint a session over it. SCOPE: the reconcile claims (conditions 1 and 2, and 1a/2a below) cover BOTH login paths. CompleteSAML, and since #2907 the OIDC login CompleteSSO, which reaches the same reconcileSSOGroups/reconcileSSORoles through syncSSOGroups/syncSSORoles and refuses the login on their error the same way (internal/core/oidc_reconcile_refusal_test.go: TestCompleteSSO_FailedGroupRemovalRefusesTheLogin, _PartialRoleReconcile_TwoOfThreeApplied, _LastAdminGroupRemovalRefused; calibrations _EmptyGroupsClaimReconcilesToZero, _AbsentGroupsClaimLeavesMembershipsAlone). OIDC presence comes from extractTokenStringList's `present`. The JIT-provisioning claims (condition 3) are pinned for CompleteSAML. #2903 review follow-ups, same tests file plus internal/core/saml_reconcile_refusal_test.go (real SQLite, persisted state read back): (1a) every refused reconcile writes exactly one FAILED audit event naming each failed step and the already-applied, not-rolled-back counts -- auth.sso_reconcile_refused, or auth.sso_reconcile_last_admin_removal_refused when the last-admin guard refused a removal (_FailedRemovalWithNothingElseToChangeIsAudited, _ReconcileReadFailureIsAudited, _PartialGroupReconcile_AddAppliedThenRemovalFails, _PartialRoleReconcile_TwoOfThreeApplied, _LastAdminGroupRemovalRefused, _LastAdminRoleRevocationRefused, calibration _AdminGroupRemovalWithASecondAdminSucceeds); (2a) a PRESENT-but-empty groups attribute reconciles to zero, an ABSENT one is a no-op (_EmptyGroupsAttributeReconcilesToZero, _AbsentGroupsAttributeLeavesMembershipsAlone; internal/saml TestExtractAssertion_GroupsPresenceIsDistinctFromEmptiness).

Startup top-up reconciliation (ADR-044), explicitly documented as additive/non-clobbering/best-effort in its own doc comment: a failure just means the next server restart retries the same reconcile. New finding via this guard's broader verb coverage.

CreateUser, then consumeInspectedToken (consume-first), then applyInvitationGrants, then UpdateProjectInvitation -- deliberately ordered (see the function's own extensive comments) with compensating reverts on BOTH failure points: a grants failure soft-deletes the orphaned account (fault-injection-proven recoverable via a resent link, Session O follow-up 2026-09-29, PR #2313 -- the coordinator's own hand-found candidate, confirmed class A at the time and fixed, not S by inspection alone), and the final race-loss path reverts via revokeInvitationGrants (unchanged, pre-existing). Reference-quality saga once fixed.

CreateProjectMembership, then (when the mode activates immediately) AddProjectMember; on a grant failure, reverts via the same revertFailedActivation helper TransitionMembership uses (audits loudly, "MANUAL CLEANUP REQUIRED", on its own failure). New finding via this guard's broader verb coverage.

F1 (ADR-110 follow-up, PR #2244) one-time backfill: AssignPermissionToRole is called once per role inside a loop, each iteration independent (a failure just logs and continues to the next role); the completion marker (SetSystemMetadata) is only set after the whole loop, so a role that didn't get granted this run is simply re-attempted on the next startup — the per-role check (`hasAlertsWrite`) already makes re-granting an already-granted role a no-op. Self-healing on retry, matching ReconcileRBACPermissions' own C classification above. seedAlertOperatorRole (called from this same function) had a genuine class-A bug — role creation and its permission grant not wrapped together, so a failure between them permanently stuck the role at zero permissions — fixed in the same PR by wrapping both in one WithTransaction, not exempted here.

Reviewed (Session O follow-up 2026-09-29, coordinator-named "worth a look"): the audit/SIEM event for a detected anomaly fires before MarkAnomalyAlertAlerted; the function's own comment explains that if marking fails, the loop retries this same anomaly on the next scheduled pass, re-emitting the SAME event -- "the audit event is already out, harmless dup". Over-alerting on failure is the safe direction (detection, not access control).

The flagged writeAuditEventFull call is `webauthn.failed` on the assertion-verification-failed early-return path -- a failure/denial event in substance, just using the generic writeAuditEventFull helper instead of writeAuditEventFailed, so the automatic method-name exclusion doesn't catch it. Same shape as the 11 auto-exempted denial events, reviewed by hand.

False positive from branch-blindness (same root cause as this function's plain write-count D entry above): the flagged writeAuditEventFull@844 ("dynamic_lease.revoke_failed") and the storage.UpdateDynamicSecretLease@852 it's compared against are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches (engine.Revoke fails vs succeeds) -- never both reached in one call.

Reviewed (Session O follow-up 2026-09-29, coordinator-named "worth a look"; body moved from RotateSecret to rotateSecret by AUDIT-MUTATION-TX-1): EventSecretRotateNoop fires after storeNextSecretVersion has ALREADY committed (a separate, earlier, already-successful write) and only states that last_rotated_at was deliberately not touched -- a claim that stays true regardless of whether the LATER c.storage.UpdateSecret call (which sets UpdatedAt, and LastRotatedAt only on the non-noop path) subsequently succeeds or fails. Not a false-success claim, unlike the #2246 LogUserCreated-before-bootstrap-commit bug this check exists to catch.

LogUserCreated@437 fires only AFTER the bootstrap transaction has already committed (txErr == nil checked first, per #2295/#2246's "Audit only AFTER the transaction has committed" comment) -- the later storage.AddPasswordHistory@449 is unrelated, best-effort post-commit bookkeeping whose failure cannot retroactively make "user created" false. Re-verify if this function's control flow changes.

LogUserCreated@222 fires only after c.CreateUser's OWN internal transaction has already committed -- the user genuinely exists at that point, and stays true regardless of a later applyInvitationGrants/UpdateProjectInvitation failure in THIS function (which now compensates via a soft-delete, PR #2313 -- a distinct, later fact, not an undo of "was created").

Confirmed real (Session O follow-up 2026-09-29, coordinator-named "worth a look"): EventSessionReuseDetected's original wording ("... -- revoking the session family") asserted an outcome before the revoke was attempted, and could still fail. Fix open: PR #2298 (reworded to state only the detected fact). Remove this line when it merges.

False positive from a shape this scan's own control-flow-blindness doc comment doesn't name: the flagged writeAuditEventFull@189 (EventSessionRevocationPanicked) is the ONLY statement inside a `defer func(){ if r := recover(); ... }()` closure wrapping the whole function body (Session Z, Z2, PR #2325's pattern applied here). A defer's body always executes strictly AFTER every earlier statement in the function -- including storage.DeleteSessionsForUserExcept@196, which the scan compares it against by raw source position, not execution order -- and only runs at all if that write already returned (normally or via panic). The audit event cannot precede the write it's compared to at runtime, regardless of where it sits in the source text.
PAT-GUARD-1: the 2 calls are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches (no PAT restriction -> MarkNotificationRead; restricted PAT -> MarkScopedNotificationRead); each is one UPDATE.

PAT-GUARD-1: the 2 calls are on MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE branches (no PAT restriction -> MarkAllNotificationsRead; restricted PAT -> MarkAllScopedNotificationsRead); each is one UPDATE, so read-all stays all-or-nothing.

SUSPEND-AUDIT-LOUD: each owed row is claimed and appended in ONE transaction (appendOwedAudit); the other writes are RecordPendingAuditEventFailure bookkeeping (attempt count, last error) on a row that stays pending. Independent per row and self-healing: a failed note leaves the row pending for the next pass, and a row is never written twice (the claim is a DELETE in the append transaction).

AUDIT-TX-3: the reissue row is now written INSIDE the transaction (fail closed, withAuditedMutation) and AddPasswordHistory is a later post-commit best-effort write by design (ADR-025, self-healing on the next password change, same as CreateUser). The audit row therefore precedes only a write that is allowed to be lost, and the row is never the unaudited-change case this guard exists for.
